name: Social Security retirement benefits
group: Federal awards by place of performance
plain: Social Security benefits paid to retired workers and their families, recorded by municipality and federal fiscal year. It is the largest federal payment to Puerto Rico households that the data can place in a municipality. It is money obligated, and part of it names no municipality.
definition: Obligations for prime awards (awards made directly to the first recipient) under assistance listing 96.002 (Social Security Retirement Insurance, Social Security Administration (SSA)) whose place of performance is in the municipality, summed over transactions dated in the federal fiscal year, in dollars of that year. The Puerto Rico value is USAspending's territory total for the listing; it also counts obligations that name no municipality.
unit: US dollars obligated in the federal fiscal year (not adjusted for inflation)
geography: 78 municipalities and Puerto Rico (USAspending's territory total, which includes obligations that name no municipality)

coverage.frequency: One value per federal fiscal year (1 October to 30 September). A year is added about six weeks after it ends, from 15 November. In the 2026-10 snapshot the file ends with FY2025.

method: economy_series.py, functions usa_programs and program_values (PROGRAMS['96.002']). For each fiscal year the build asks the USAspending 'spending by geography' service for prime awards with program_numbers [96.002], once at the county layer for the 78 municipality codes and once at the state layer for PR. Unplaced share = (Puerto Rico - sum of the 78) / Puerto Rico x 100, at least 0, rounded to 0.1, stored in economy_series.json under extras.statewide_share.fed_prog_ss_retirement. A listing is mapped, and a year kept, only when it passes the placement rule of HANDOFF decision 69: at least 20 municipalities with money, under 40% of the placed money in San Juan and at most 50% naming no municipality. A series keeps the latest unbroken run of years that pass (kept_years). The checks, their sensitivity to the thresholds and a comparison with SSA's county tables are in docs/analysis/public-money-v2-2026-10.
source_detail: USAspending.gov, search service 'spending by geography' (api.usaspending.gov/api/v2/search/spending_by_geography/): scope place_of_performance, filter program_numbers [96.002], county layer for the 78 municipality codes and state layer for PR, prime awards only (subawards off), federal fiscal years 2012 to 2025, retrieved 2026-10-31.
how_to_read: In the 2026-10 snapshot (USAspending, retrieved 2026-10-31), Puerto Rico's value for FY2025 is $8.86 billion, against $4.28 billion in FY2012. In FY2025, 78 of the 78 municipalities have a value; the largest are San Juan ($1.18 billion), Bayamón ($573.4 million), Carolina ($438.8 million). In every year from FY2012 to FY2025, USAspending places all of Puerto Rico's money for this listing in a municipality. Compare municipalities per resident.
caveats: The Social Security Administration reports these benefits to USAspending as aggregated records (one per place and period, not per person). They follow where beneficiaries live: each municipality's share of the FY2025 money matches its share of the benefits in SSA's own county table for December 2024 (correlation 1.0, largest gap 0.04 percentage points, Mayagüez), and FY2014 matches December 2013 (correlation 0.9971, largest gap 0.58 points). SSA's table, OASDI Beneficiaries by State and County, counts beneficiaries by county of residence.

Fiscal years 2008 to 2011 are left out under the placement rule of HANDOFF decision 69: in FY2008 to FY2011 San Juan holds 54% to 100% of the money placed. The agency recorded the money centrally in those years, so a map would show where it was recorded, not where it went.

In the 2026-10 snapshot, of the 1,092 municipality-year cells (14 years, 78 municipalities), 0 are blank (no obligation recorded there) and 0 are negative (downward corrections larger than the year's new obligations). A blank is not proof that no one there received the program.

The seven programs the observatory maps are 39.7% of all federal awards to Puerto Rico in FY2025 (17.6% to 39.7% over FY2021 to FY2025). The rest, including Medicaid, nutrition assistance, highways and most disaster and COVID money, is not mapped by program because USAspending names no municipality for it or records it where the Commonwealth agency is, in San Juan (HANDOFF decision 69).
This is money obligated (committed) in the fiscal year, as USAspending reports it. It is not the same as money paid (outlays), and a year's value can change when agencies correct their records.

The Puerto Rico value is USAspending's total for the territory, which also counts obligations that name no municipality, so it is larger than the sum of the 78 municipalities. The share that cannot be placed is listed by year in the dataset's information window (extras.statewide_share).
Federal fiscal years run from 1 October to 30 September: FY2024 is October 2023 to September 2024.
Values are in dollars of each year, not adjusted for inflation.
Do not add this series to economy.fed_direct_payments or economy.fed_awards_total: those already include it.

coverage.frequency: One value per federal fiscal year (1 October to 30 September). A year is added about six weeks after it ends, from 15 November. In the 2026-10 snapshot the file ends with FY2025.

method: economy_series.py, functions usa_programs and program_values (PROGRAMS['14.195']). For each fiscal year the build asks the USAspending 'spending by geography' service for prime awards with program_numbers [14.195], once at the county layer for the 78 municipality codes and once at the state layer for PR. Unplaced share = (Puerto Rico - sum of the 78) / Puerto Rico x 100, at least 0, rounded to 0.1, stored in economy_series.json under extras.statewide_share.fed_prog_pbra. A listing is mapped, and a year kept, only when it passes the placement rule of HANDOFF decision 69: at least 20 municipalities with money, under 40% of the placed money in San Juan and at most 50% naming no municipality. A series keeps the latest unbroken run of years that pass (kept_years). The checks, their sensitivity to the thresholds and a comparison with SSA's county tables are in docs/analysis/public-money-v2-2026-10.
source_detail: USAspending.gov, search service 'spending by geography' (api.usaspending.gov/api/v2/search/spending_by_geography/): scope place_of_performance, filter program_numbers [14.195], county layer for the 78 municipality codes and state layer for PR, prime awards only (subawards off), federal fiscal years 2019 to 2025, retrieved 2026-10-31.
how_to_read: In the 2026-10 snapshot (USAspending, retrieved 2026-10-31), Puerto Rico's value for FY2025 is $150.5 million, against $130.7 million in FY2019. In FY2025, 44 of the 78 municipalities have a value; the largest are San Juan ($53.9 million), Caguas ($12.3 million), Bayamón ($11.7 million). In every year from FY2019 to FY2025, USAspending places all of Puerto Rico's money for this listing in a municipality. Compare municipalities per resident.
caveats: Placed where the assisted building is. A municipality without a Section 8 project-based building has no value. HUD's housing choice vouchers (listing 14.871) are a different program and are not in this series.

Fiscal years 2008 to 2018 are left out under the placement rule of HANDOFF decision 69: in FY2008 to FY2009 most or all of the money names no municipality; in FY2010 to FY2018 San Juan holds 54% to 84% of the money placed. The agency recorded the money centrally in those years, so a map would show where it was recorded, not where it went.

In the 2026-10 snapshot, of the 546 municipality-year cells (7 years, 78 municipalities), 235 are blank (no obligation recorded there) and 0 are negative (downward corrections larger than the year's new obligations). A blank is not proof that no one there received the program.

The seven programs the observatory maps are 39.7% of all federal awards to Puerto Rico in FY2025 (17.6% to 39.7% over FY2021 to FY2025). The rest, including Medicaid, nutrition assistance, highways and most disaster and COVID money, is not mapped by program because USAspending names no municipality for it or records it where the Commonwealth agency is, in San Juan (HANDOFF decision 69).
This is money obligated (committed) in the fiscal year, as USAspending reports it. It is not the same as money paid (outlays), and a year's value can change when agencies correct their records.

The Puerto Rico value is USAspending's total for the territory, which also counts obligations that name no municipality, so it is larger than the sum of the 78 municipalities. The share that cannot be placed is listed by year in the dataset's information window (extras.statewide_share).
Federal fiscal years run from 1 October to 30 September: FY2024 is October 2023 to September 2024.
Values are in dollars of each year, not adjusted for inflation.
Do not add this series to economy.fed_direct_payments or economy.fed_awards_total: those already include it. USAspending records this program as a direct payment for a specified use, not as a grant.

view.label: Map, Analysis tab (group Public money): shade municipalities by dollars per resident
